title: Smoke, Stools and Stories: Why Street Food Wins Hearts
title_zh: 炊烟、小凳与故事：街头美食为何赢得人心
intro_zh: 本文约 556 词，共 9 段，从价格、感官、社交、食材与近年变化等角度介绍街头美食的魅力，包含曼谷摊贩数量、墨西哥街角塔可、曼谷唐人街与河内老城区等具体事例，并配 4 道 CET-4 阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: Every evening, in cities from Bangkok to Mexico City, the smell of grilled meat and fresh bread drifts through the streets. Long before restaurants open their doors, small carts and stalls are already busy. Street food is not just a quick meal; it is one of the most direct ways to taste a city's culture.
paragraphs.zh: 每天傍晚，从曼谷到墨西哥城，烤肉的香味和新鲜面包的气息在街头飘散。早在餐馆开门之前，小小的推车和摊位就已经忙碌起来。街头美食不只是快速填饱肚子的一餐，它是品尝一座城市文化最直接的方式之一。

paragraphs.en: Bangkok may be the world's street-food capital. According to local guides, the city has more than 100,000 street vendors, and many of them sell the same dish for decades. A bowl of noodles there often costs less than two dollars, which is why office workers, students and tourists all eat side by side on the same plastic stools.
paragraphs.zh: 曼谷也许是世界街头美食之都。据当地导游介绍，这座城市有超过 10 万名街头摊贩，其中许多人几十年来一直卖同一道菜。那里一碗面常常不到两美元，因此上班族、学生和游客会并排坐在同样的塑料凳上吃饭。

paragraphs.en: Mexico offers another famous example. Tacos sold from a corner stand usually come with fresh onions, coriander and lime, and the cook prepares them in front of you in less than a minute. This speed matters: street food is designed for people who are walking, chatting or waiting for a bus. In some neighborhoods, the same family has sold the same recipe for three generations, and regular customers know exactly what to order.
paragraphs.zh: 墨西哥提供了另一个著名的例子。街角摊位卖的塔可通常配上新鲜的洋葱、香菜和青柠，摊主不到一分钟就能在你面前做好。这种速度很重要：街头美食是为那些正在走路、聊天或等公交车的人准备的。在一些街区，同一个家族三代人都在卖同一份配方，老顾客清楚知道自己要点什么。

paragraphs.en: One reason street food survives is its price. A vendor has no rent for a large dining room and no expensive furniture, so the cost of an affordable meal stays low. For many families in Asia, Africa and Latin America, these small businesses are also a first step into the economy, requiring little money to start but offering a daily income.
paragraphs.zh: 街头美食能延续下来的一个原因是价格。摊贩不用为宽敞的餐厅付租金，也没有昂贵的家具，因此一顿实惠饭菜的成本能保持很低。对亚洲、非洲和拉丁美洲的许多家庭来说，这些小生意也是踏入经济生活的第一步：启动资金不多，却能带来每天的收入。

paragraphs.en: But cheap food alone cannot explain its charm. Street food speaks to the senses first. The aroma of spices, the sound of oil in a hot pan, the bright colors of fruit on a wooden tray — each one promises a strong flavor. Watching a cook work is part of the pleasure; the meal begins before the first bite.
paragraphs.zh: 但仅凭便宜并不能解释它的魅力。街头美食首先打动的是感官。香料的香气、热锅里油的声音、木盘上水果的鲜亮色彩——每一样都预示着一股浓郁的风味。看厨师操作本身就是乐趣的一部分；这一餐在第一口之前就已经开始了。

paragraphs.en: The atmosphere is social as well. Strangers share a long table, argue about which stall is best, and recommend dishes to visitors. In many places the market at night becomes a meeting point for the whole neighborhood, a place where grandparents and teenagers eat the same food. In Bangkok's Chinatown or in Hanoi's old quarter, a single street may hold thirty stalls, each specializing in one dish.
paragraphs.zh: 这里的氛围也是社交性的。陌生人共用一张长桌，争论哪家摊位最好，还向游客推荐菜品。在许多地方，夜市成为整个社区的聚会点，祖辈和青少年在那里吃着同样的食物。在曼谷的唐人街或河内的老城区，一条街上可能有三十个摊位，每个都专做一道菜。

paragraphs.en: Fresh ingredients are another draw. Because vendors buy in small amounts and cook quickly, vegetables and meat often arrive the same morning. A cook who uses yesterday's fish will lose customers fast, so quality is protected by the crowd itself. Language is rarely a problem either, because pointing at a dish and smiling usually works.
paragraphs.zh: 新鲜的食材是另一个吸引力。因为摊贩每次进货量小、做菜又快，蔬菜和肉常常当天早上才到。用昨天鱼肉的摊主很快就会失去顾客，所以质量是由食客自己守护的。语言也很少成为障碍，指着菜笑一笑通常就够了。

paragraphs.en: Street food is changing too. In cities such as Singapore and Portland, food trucks now use apps to tell customers where they will park, and some young cooks mix traditional recipes with new ideas. Health rules have become stricter, which costs money but also makes eating on the street safer than it was twenty years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 街头美食也在变化。在新加坡、波特兰这样的城市，餐车现在用手机应用告诉顾客自己会停在哪里，一些年轻厨师把传统配方和新想法结合起来。卫生规定变得更严格，这虽然增加了成本，却也让街头饮食比二十年前更安全。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps that is the real charm of street food. It is simple, honest and open to everyone, rich or poor, local or foreign. One small paper plate can carry centuries of cooking skill, and the story of a city is served with it. So the next time you travel, skip the hotel restaurant once and follow the smoke and the noise. You may remember that three-dollar meal longer than anything else on the trip.
paragraphs.zh: 也许这正是街头美食真正的魅力。它简单、真诚，向所有人开放，无论贫富，无论本地人还是外国人。一只小小的纸盘能承载数百年的烹饪技艺，一座城市的故事也随之端上桌。所以下次旅行时，不妨一次跳过酒店餐厅，跟着炊烟和喧闹走。你或许会记得那顿三美元的饭，比旅途中的任何东西都久。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to open a small food business in a big city.
Why street food attracts people in different parts of the world.
The health risks of eating meals cooked outdoors.
A comparison of restaurant prices in Asia and Latin America.
questions.explain: 全文从价格、感官体验、社交氛围、食材新鲜度和近年变化等方面解释街头美食为何受欢迎，并举出曼谷、墨西哥城、新加坡等例子，因此主旨是 B。A、C、D 都只是文中某个细节或文中未强调的内容。

questions.q: According to paragraph 4, why can street vendors keep their prices low?
options: They receive money from the local government.
They buy all their food from large supermarkets.
They pay no rent for a big dining room or costly furniture.
They sell only one dish and cook it in large amounts.
questions.explain: 第 4 段明确说摊贩没有大餐厅的租金，也没有昂贵家具，所以实惠饭菜的成本很低，故选 C。文中没有提到政府补贴（A）、超市采购（B）或只卖一道菜（D）。

questions.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 7 about food quality at street stalls?
options: Vendors seldom care whether their food is fresh.
The daily choices of customers help keep the food fresh.
Officials check every stall early each morning.
Vegetables are usually stored for several days before cooking.
questions.explain: 第 7 段说摊贩进货量小、当天早上到货，用隔夜鱼的摊主会很快失去顾客，因此质量由食客自身守护，可推知顾客每天的选择促使摊主保持新鲜，故选 B。A、D 与原文相反，C 文中未提。

questions.q: The word 'draw' in paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 原文 'Fresh ingredients are another draw' 意为“新鲜食材是另一个吸引力”，draw 在此作名词表示吸引人的事物，与 attraction 最接近，故选 A。picture（图画）、problem（问题）、rule（规则）均不符合语境。
